title: Between and among
subtitle: between her thumb and forefinger / among all his friends
summary: Use between for separate individuals, comparisons, choices and agreements, and among for groups, and learn the fixed expressions built on each.

lesson.heading: Separate things or a group?

left.label: between - people or things seen as individual or separate
examples: She held the diamond **between** her thumb and forefinger.
Zimbabwe is situated **between** Zambia to the north, Mozambique to the east, Botswana to the west, and South Africa to the south.

right.label: among - part of a group or mass
right.text: Among is only used with three or more people or things.
examples: He stood **among** all his friends at the party and felt very happy.
She eventually found her passport **among** the clothes in the drawer.

lesson.note: Amongst is sometimes used instead of among, but in more literary contexts.

lesson.heading: Dividing and sharing: either word
lesson.text: Between and among are not only prepositions of place. For something divided or shared between people we can use either.

examples.text: The money is to be divided **between** / **among** the towns in the area.
The prize will be shared **between** / **among** the first six finishers in the race.

lesson.heading: between for comparisons and relationships
lesson.text: We use **between** to talk about comparisons and relationships.

examples.text: There should be a better balance on the committee **between** the various ethnic groups.
They are wrong to claim that there is a link **between** unemployment and crime.

lesson.note: Also with between: association, comparison, connection, contrast, correlation, difference, distinction, relationship.

lesson.heading: between for choices
lesson.text: We use **between** when we talk about choices.

examples.text: I have to choose **between** the universities of Leeds, York and Manchester.
He felt torn **between** his family and his friends.

lesson.heading: between for agreements and shared amounts
lesson.text: We use **between** for discussions, or the results of discussions, when we name the two or more people or groups involved, and to say that people or things share an amount of something.

examples.text: There was a disagreement **between** Emma, Jade and Zoe.
The treaty was signed **between** Great Britain and France.
**Between** them, Will and Alice must earn about 100,000 a year.
Last year the three companies built 30,000 houses **between** them.

lesson.heading: among for groups
lesson.text: We use **among** to mean 'existing or happening in a particular group', and to mean 'included in a particular group'.

examples.text: The disease has now broken out **among** the hill tribes.
Their music is still very popular **among** teenagers.
They are **among** the best hockey players in the world.
**Among** the capital cities of South America, Quito is the second highest.

lesson.heading: Common expressions
lesson.text: A number of fixed expressions use these two words.

examples.text: The concert features, **among others**, Karl Frisk and the Johnsons.
examples.note: = other singers / groups are featured too

examples.text: I later found out that he had been a carpenter and a plumber, **among other things**.
examples.note: = he had had other jobs too

examples.text: **Between ourselves** / **Between you and me**, I don't think Jack is as honest as he should be.

lesson.text: If you could name the items one by one, use between; if they blur into a crowd or a mass, use among.

exercises.prompt: For a couple of days I've had a pain ___ my shoulder blades.
He couldn't find a microphone ___ all the recording equipment he had with him.
exercises.explanation: The equipment is a mass of things, so among.
Two people we see as individuals, so between.

exercises.prompt: The lost manuscript was discovered ___ the thousands of books in the cellar.
exercises.explanation: Thousands of books form a mass, so among.

exercises.prompt: Rebecca commutes ___ her flat in Paris and her office in Brussels.
The distinction ___ and professional athletes is becoming less clear.
exercises.explanation: Distinction is one of the comparison nouns that take between.

exercises.prompt: It has become fashionable ___ to dye their hair in various colours.
exercises.explanation: Among means 'existing or happening in a particular group'.

exercises.prompt: Given a choice ___ and washing up, I know which I'd prefer to do.

exercises.statement: He stood between all his friends at the party and felt very happy.
exercises.explanation: He stood among all his friends at the party. His friends are a group, so among.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to say that three companies shared a total.
exercises.answer: Last year the three companies built 30,000 houses between them.
exercises.explanation: Between them says that the group shares one amount.

exercises.prompt: Keira is writing home from Rome. Which word fits each gap?

items.text: There is such an incredible contrast ___ the old parts of the city and the more recent parts.
But ___ you and me, I'm a bit scared of heights.
The Pantheon is ___ the Vatican and the Foro Romano.
The only problem then was choosing ___ the many different types of pasta!
Rome must be ___ the most fascinating cities in the world.
Yesterday we visited, ___ other places, the Foro Romano and the Vatican.
Umberto I and the artist Raphael are ___ the people buried there.

exercises.prompt: Match each expression with what it tells you.

pairs.left: The concert features, among others, Karl Frisk and the Johnsons.
pairs.right: Other singers and groups are featured too.

pairs.left: He had been a carpenter and a plumber, among other things.
pairs.right: He had had other jobs as well.

pairs.left: Between ourselves, I don't think Jack is as honest as he should be.
Between them, Will and Alice must earn about 100,000 a year.
He felt torn between his family and his friends.
pairs.right: He had to choose between two sides.
